options.label: Support blocker
options.meaning: A region intended to prevent support generation where it intersects. It does not make an unsupported overhang printable without support.

options.label: Support enforcer
options.meaning: A region intended to request support. Other support eligibility and geometry rules may still matter; verify the preview rather than assuming support appears everywhere.

options.label: Internal mask
options.meaning: Selects the internal-mask class. The precise roles and boundary treatment affected are unresolved in this survey; do not assume it cuts a cavity or changes a tool.

options.label: Full mask
options.meaning: Selects the full-mask class. Its exact difference from internal mask is not verified; do not assume it removes the model or applies every setting throughout it.

fields.meaning: Chooses what a modifier or mask region is intended to affect. A mask is an auxiliary region, not automatically a printable part.
fields.when_to_change: When deliberately restricting support or applying a documented regional modifier, not during a basic material comparison.
fields.effect: Changing the class can change which toolpaths are permitted in the region. It does not simply change the colour of the region.
fields.caution: Internal-mask versus full-mask coverage is not established by these labels; inspect the resulting preview. The option names below are source labels, not a live visibility guarantee.
fields.status: Schema-backed selector; partly interpreted; mask-class details unverified.

fields.caution: A temperature field is not a plate or material rating. Do not use bed heat to compensate for a loose plate or leaking hotend.
fields.status: Functional interpretation; physical result unvalidated.

options.label: Line

options.label: Grid

options.label: Zigzag
options.meaning: Back-and-forth fill joined where the geometry permits. It reduces separate line starts compared with disconnected lines.

options.label: Concentric
options.meaning: Nested paths following the region's outline. Useful when following contours matters; inspect narrow centers and corners.

options.label: Honeycomb
options.meaning: A cellular pattern based on hexagonal cells. It creates repeated cell walls rather than long parallel fill lines.

options.label: Tri-Hexagon
options.meaning: A pattern combining triangular and hexagonal regions. It changes cell geometry compared with a simple grid or honeycomb.

options.label: Gyroid
options.meaning: A smoothly varying three-dimensional periodic infill pattern. Layer shapes change through the height rather than repeating one flat grid.

options.label: 3D Honeycomb
options.meaning: A honeycomb-style cellular structure that changes through the height. Inspect successive layers rather than judging it from one layer.

options.label: Cubic
options.meaning: A three-dimensional, cube-derived lattice. Its cross-section changes with height and distributes paths across several directions.

options.label: Crosshatch
options.meaning: A crossing-line hatch pattern. It changes the line arrangement and junction layout; compare the actual paths with Grid before choosing.

options.label: Diamond

options.label: Neovius

options.label: Lidinoid
